title: Distributional lower bound for public-coin complexity
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a target function, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, let $n \in \bbn$, and let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$. Suppose that every deterministic protocol $p$ whose communication complexity is at most $n$ has distributional error strictly greater than $\varepsilon$ against $f$ under $\mu$; that is, the $\mu$-probability that $p$ disagrees with $f$ exceeds $\varepsilon$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ is strictly greater than $n$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α is the target function
μ is a finite probability space on X × Y

replaced:
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let
$\mu$ be a finite probability distribution on $X \times Y$.  If every deterministic
protocol $p$ with $p.\mathrm{complexity} \le n$ satisfies
$p.\mathrm{distributionalError}(\mu, f) > \varepsilon$, then the public-coin randomized
communication complexity of $f$ at error $\varepsilon$ is strictly greater than $n$.
This is one direction of Yao's minimax principle: a hard distribution for all small
deterministic protocols certifies a lower bound on randomized complexity.
